title: Birán to Santa Ifigenia: the Lawyer, the Sierra, and the Stone with One Word
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Finca Manacas, Birán: the birth of a cook's son
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: On his father's cane estate in the foothills of the Nipe mountains, Lina Ruz Gonzalez bears a son to Angel Castro y Argiz, a Galician who came to Cuba as a conscript in Spain's last colonial war and stayed to buy land. The child is born out of wedlock to the household cook, and for years he is not registered under his father's name. Around him the finca runs on Haitian and Jamaican cutters, a company store, and a spur of track feeding the United Fruit line. He will not be baptized until he is eight years old.
suggested_refs: The preserved Finca Manacas at Biran, now a state historical site

stops.name: Colegio de Dolores, Santiago de Cuba: the baptism and the Jesuits
stops.date_confidence: year approximate; the pool's range 1935-1941 is wrong at both ends and omits La Salle. Wikipedia has him baptized aged eight (so 1935, not the pool's 1934), boarded at La Salle first, and only later transferred to Dolores, which he leaves for Belen in 1942
stops.campa: Sent from the finca at six to board with his primary teacher, the boy waits three more years for the water. He is baptized at eight, then put into the La Salle school, then handed to the Jesuits of the Colegio de Dolores. The fathers give him Latin, rhetoric, and a habit of argument built to be spoken aloud rather than written down. He is rich enough to be sent and provincial enough to be mocked for it, and the Oriente accent follows him into every classroom. He will credit the Jesuits with his discipline for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: The Jesuit Colegio de Dolores near Parque Cespedes, Santiago de Cuba

stops.name: Colegio de Belen, Marianao: the school of the sugar barons
stops.date_confidence: attested as the year of transfer; the school years run 1942-1945
stops.campa: He transfers to the Colegio de Belen in Marianao, the Jesuit school of the Havana rich, and takes it by force of body: basketball, baseball, track, the mountains climbed on school expeditions. He is a provincial scholarship among the sons of mill owners and cabinet ministers. The 1945 yearbook says his life will be filled with brilliant pages, a line quoted for seventy years and reproduced nowhere. He leaves Marianao at eighteen speaking like a seminarian and built like an athlete.
suggested_refs: The Marianao campus of the Colegio de Belen, later the Instituto Tecnico Militar

stops.name: University of Havana: the law faculty and the pistols
stops.date_confidence: attested year of enrolment; the pool's coordinate 23.1367 / -82.3666 was 1.6 km east of the campus and has been corrected to the Vedado hill
stops.campa: He climbs the steps into a law faculty that settles its politics with pistols. The action groups of the postwar university, half revolutionary and half racket, recruit him inside a year; he carries a gun to class and is named in shootings he denies. He joins the Ortodoxos of Eduardo Chibas, who campaigns against corruption with a broom for a symbol. He spends five years on this hill, among the crowds and the factions, and in September 1950 he takes the degree of Doctor of Law.
suggested_refs: The escalinata and Alma Mater statue of the University of Havana, Vedado

stops.name: Cayo Confites, Camaguey: the expedition against Trujillo
stops.date_confidence: month contested: Wikipedia says the force intended to sail in July 1947, while its Caribbean Legion coverage dates the arrest of the roughly 1,200 men to September 1947. Neither reading is adopted over the other
stops.campa: On a cay off the northern Camaguey coast some twelve hundred men gather to sail against Rafael Trujillo of the Dominican Republic, and the law student from Havana is among them. The Caribbean Legion has money, aircraft, and no permission. Washington leans on President Grau, the Cuban government breaks the expedition up, and the men are taken. By his own account, told often afterward and by no one else, Castro swims ashore across the bay of Nipe rather than surrender. It is his first armed expedition by sea. The second one lands.
suggested_refs: The Sabana-Camaguey cays, mustering ground of the 1947 expedition

stops.name: Bogota: the Bogotazo
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: He arrives at twenty-one with a Cuban student delegation, sent to hold a counter-congress against the Pan-American conference meeting in the same city. On the ninth of April Jorge Eliecer Gaitan is shot in the street and the capital burns for three days. Castro takes a rifle from a police station and goes into the crowds; the Colombian government afterward lists him among the foreign agitators. He goes home having watched an insurrection with no plan behind it and no one in command of it.
suggested_refs: The corner of Carrera Septima where Gaitan was shot, 9 April 1948

stops.name: Havana: the marriage to Mirta Diaz-Balart
stops.date_confidence: year attested, month inferred from the New York honeymoon of October 1948; the pool gives no day
stops.campa: He marries Mirta Diaz-Balart, a philosophy student from a wealthy Oriente family whose father is a lawyer for United Fruit and whose brother will hold office under Batista. Batista sends a wedding gift. The couple spend three months in New York, where Castro reads and considers studying at Columbia until the money runs out; no source names the hotel. Their son Fidel Angel is born the following September. The marriage lasts six years and ends while he is in prison.
sources: Robert E. Quirk, 'Fidel Castro' (for the New York stay; not consulted directly)
suggested_refs: The Diaz-Balart and Castro families of Banes, Oriente, joined and split in six years

stops.name: Havana: Chibas at the microphone and Batista at the gate
stops.date_confidence: the coup is attested to the day; the Chibas suicide is attested by the pool to 1951 only, without month
stops.campa: Eduardo Chibas, whose Sunday radio hour is the conscience of the republic, shoots himself at the microphone at the end of a broadcast and dies days later. Castro is at the hospital and at the funeral. The elections Chibas was to contest are set for June; Castro is standing for congress. On the tenth of March Batista walks into Camp Columbia before dawn, takes the presidency without a shot, and cancels the vote. Castro files a brief arguing that the constitution obliges citizens to rebel. The court does not answer it.
suggested_refs: Eduardo Chibas's last broadcast, CMQ radio, Havana, August 1951

stops.name: Moncada Barracks, Santiago de Cuba: the assault
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: During the carnival of Santiago, in borrowed army uniforms, a column of cars drives on the second largest garrison in Cuba. The sources put the raiders at a hundred and thirty-five or at a hundred and sixty-five and do not agree. The lead car takes a wrong turn, the sentries wake, and the thing collapses in twenty minutes. Six rebels fall in the fighting; twenty-two are tortured and shot in the yard afterward. Castro is taken in the hills six days later by a lieutenant who refuses the order to kill him.
stops.quote: You may be victorious or defeated in a few hours, but hear this well, comrades!
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, address to the combatants before leaving for the Moncada Barracks, Santiago de Cuba, 26 July 1953 (Marxists Internet Archive translation)
sources: Marxists Internet Archive, Castro archive, 26 July 1953
suggested_refs: The bullet-marked wall of the Moncada Barracks, now the Ciudad Escolar 26 de Julio

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: history will absolve me
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the sentencing; the trial had opened at the Palace of Justice on 21 September 1953
stops.campa: Tried apart from his comrades in a nurses' room at the civil hospital, the accused conducts his own defense and turns the dock into a platform. He speaks for something near two hours, indicting the hunger of six hundred thousand unemployed Cubans and the illiteracy of the countryside, and closes with a sentence that will be painted on walls. He is given fifteen years. No stenographic record survives. The speech the world reads is the one he rebuilds from memory in prison the following year and smuggles out in lemon juice between the lines of letters.
stops.quote: Condemn me. It does not matter. History will absolve me.
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, closing line of the defense speech at his trial, Santiago de Cuba, 16 October 1953; Speakola transcript and Fidel Castro Reader (Ocean Press), p. 105, where the punctuation differs by translator
sources: Speakola, 'Fidel Castro: speech from the dock', 16 October 1953
Wikiquote, citing Fidel Castro Reader (Ocean Press) p. 105
suggested_refs: The 1954 clandestine pamphlet La historia me absolvera, printed by El Curita at Plaza del Vapor

stops.name: Presidio Modelo, Isla de Pinos: the movement takes its name
stops.date_confidence: the year is attested for the prison studies and the renaming; the pool gives no month, defaulted to January
stops.campa: In the circular panopticon on the Isle of Pines the prisoners keep a school they call the Abel Santamaria Academy: history, philosophy, political economy, taught in shifts. He reads Marti and Marx and Lenin, writes every day, and renames the conspiracy the 26th of July Movement after the day it failed. Mirta is found on a government payroll her name was placed on without her knowledge; the scandal reaches him inside and the marriage ends. He will leave this island with a name for the thing, a pamphlet, and no wife.
suggested_refs: The circular cellblocks of the Presidio Modelo, Isla de la Juventud

stops.name: Presidio Modelo: the amnesty
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: A press campaign, public pressure, and Batista's confidence in his own position produce a general amnesty, and after twenty-two months the Moncada prisoners walk out through the gate. Batista has calculated that a freed prisoner is worth less to the opposition than a martyr. Castro tells reporters that he does not intend to stay in a country where he can neither speak nor write, and within seven weeks he is gone. The government that opened the gate will spend four years announcing that he is dead, and believing it.
suggested_refs: The amnesty law of May 1955 and the release of the Moncada prisoners

stops.name: Mexico City: the apartment on Calle Emparan
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month by the corpus interlock; the pool gives no day
stops.campa: Raul brings his brother to the apartment of Maria Antonia Gonzalez on Calle Emparan, where an Argentine doctor with asthma has been living at the edge of the exile colony. Fidel Castro and Ernesto Guevara talk through the night, and by dawn Guevara has signed on as the expedition's physician, third confirmed member after the two brothers. Castro tours Florida and New York collecting money from Cuban exiles. Colonel Alberto Bayo, veteran of the Spanish republic, drills the recruits on a ranch outside Chalco.
suggested_refs: Emparan 49, Mexico City, where Castro and Guevara first met

stops.name: Tuxpan, Veracruz: the Granma casts off
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and the hour, two in the morning
stops.campa: In rain, at two in the morning, eighty-two men board a sixty-foot cabin cruiser refitted after the war to sleep twelve, and drop down the Tuxpan river with the lights out. Castro has promised in print that in 1956 he will be free or a martyr, and the calendar has five days left in November. Guevara is aboard as the expedition doctor, Raul as a lieutenant. The boat rides low, loaded past its marks with men and rifles and too little fuel, and the crossing that should take five days will take seven.
suggested_refs: The Granma, preserved under glass at the Museo de la Revolucion, Havana

stops.name: Playa Las Coloradas: not a landing but a shipwreck
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the coordinate is approximate, the pool's two competing pins being 20 km inland and 9 km south of the Niquero coast
stops.campa: The Granma misses its landfall and grounds in mangrove shallows on the west-facing coast of Niquero, two days late for the rising that was meant to meet it. The men wade ashore through swamp, leaving the heavy weapons and the whole schedule behind them; one of them says afterward that it was not a landing but a shipwreck. Batista's aircraft are over them within hours. The rising Frank Pais timed to the landing has already been fought in Santiago and lost. They walk east through cane toward mountains none of them has seen.
suggested_refs: Desembarco del Granma National Park, Niquero, Granma province

stops.name: Alegria de Pio: the ambush in the cane
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and to roughly four in the afternoon; the pool's coordinate was 14 km too far north and has been corrected
stops.campa: Three days ashore, worn out and given away by a guide, the column stops to rest in a cane field and the army finds it at four in the afternoon. The party is shot apart. Guevara, hit in the neck, chooses a box of ammunition over the medical kit. Of the eighty-two, some counts give twelve survivors and some twenty-two, and the accounts will never agree. Castro lies days in the cane, then reaches the farm of Ramon Perez at Cinco Palmas, finds his brother alive, is told seven rifles are left, and says that now they have won the war.
suggested_refs: The monument at Alegria de Pio, Granma province

stops.name: La Plata, Sierra Maestra: the first victory
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the coordinate is approximate, the garrison site not independently pinpointed
stops.campa: With a dozen rifles and guides from the mountain villages, the survivors come down on a coastal-guard post at the mouth of the La Plata river before dawn and take it, killing two and carrying off weapons and medicine. The whole value of the action is that it happened: the peasants of the Sierra learn that the men the newspapers buried are alive and shooting. Castro orders the wounded soldiers treated and released. He will keep that policy for two years and publicize it without pause.
suggested_refs: The mouth of the La Plata river, first rebel action of the Sierra campaign

stops.name: Sierra Maestra: Herbert Matthews finds a living man
stops.date_confidence: the pool attests the year only; February follows the conventional dating of the interview to 17 February 1957 and is not attested in the reachable source
stops.campa: Herbert Matthews of the New York Times is walked up the mountain in the dark and interviewed at first light in a clearing, with the same few men marched past him twice to suggest numbers the column does not have. The piece runs on the front page in three parts and kills the government's claim that Castro died at the landing. From this week the war is fought in two places at once, in the Sierra and in the American press, and a column that cannot yet win a battle is winning the front page.
suggested_refs: Herbert Matthews's three-part dispatch, The New York Times, February 1957

stops.name: El Uvero: the sawmill barracks
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the pool's coordinate was 45 km too far west and has been corrected
stops.campa: The column, grown to something over a hundred, attacks the army barracks at a coastal sawmill settlement in full daylight and holds the fight for two and a half hours, the heaviest casualties on both sides so far. Guevara calls it the coming of age of the guerrilla. Doctors are taken with the barracks and set to work on the wounded of both armies. After El Uvero the army pulls its small posts back off this coast, and for the first time the rebels hold a continuous stretch of mountain rather than hiding in one.
suggested_refs: The sawmill settlement of El Uvero on the Sierra Maestra coast

stops.name: La Comandancia de la Plata: the state under the canopy
stops.date_confidence: the headquarters is attested for the war's last year but not to a founding day; January is the house default. The 1957 ascent of Pico Turquino, recorded in the same campa, is attested to the year only
stops.campa: On a ridge under closed forest canopy, invisible from the air, the rebels put up sixteen wooden houses: a hospital, a press for El Cubano Libre, a workshop, a kitchen, and the transmitter of Radio Rebelde. Castro's hut has a trapdoor and a view of every approach. Guevara has already built the first such settlement at El Hombrito. Somewhere in 1957 the column climbs Pico Turquino, the highest ground in Cuba, where a bust of Jose Marti has stood since his centenary. The summer offensive will throw ten thousand soldiers at this ridge and fail.
sources: Cuban National Monument records for La Comandancia de la Plata (second hand)
suggested_refs: La Comandancia de la Plata, national monument, Sierra Maestra

stops.name: Sierra Maestra: the order that creates Column 8
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the corpus interlock
stops.campa: By written order Castro creates Column 8 and gives it to Guevara, with instructions to cross four hundred kilometers of open country into Las Villas and cut the island in half. Camilo Cienfuegos takes a second column north. The mountain empties of its best men and the war leaves the Sierra for the plain. Castro stays in Oriente, running by radio and courier a war now fought in three provinces and negotiating with the civil opposition in exile for a legitimacy he intends to keep in his own hands. Santa Clara falls four months later.
suggested_refs: Castro's written order of 21 August 1958 constituting Column 8

stops.name: Santa Clara: Batista goes, the columns are sent
stops.date_confidence: attested to the night of 31 December 1958 into 1 January 1959
stops.campa: Guevara's column derails an armored train and takes the provincial capital, and on the last night of the year Batista boards an aircraft at Camp Columbia with his family and, by one account, more than three hundred million dollars. Castro hears of the flight by radio in Oriente. He refuses the junta the generals propose, calls a general strike, and orders both columns down the central highway to Havana at once, so that no one else can take the capital. Cienfuegos and Guevara enter it on the second of January.
suggested_refs: The derailed armored train at Santa Clara, preserved as a monument

stops.name: Santiago de Cuba: the revolution begins now
stops.date_confidence: contested across three days: the pool's chronology lens gives 1 and 2 January for the entry and speech, its quotes lens dates the Cespedes Park address to 3 January. Nothing reachable adjudicates, and the stop is placed at the earliest of the three
stops.campa: The garrison of Santiago surrenders without a shot and Castro walks into the city his revolution has carried in its name since Moncada. He speaks from the balcony over Cespedes Park, declares Santiago the provisional capital, and tells the crowd that this time the victory will not be taken out of Cuban hands by a foreign fleet as it was in 1898. The date of the speech is unsettled between sources. The man on the balcony holds no office of any kind and is already governing.
stops.quote: We have finally reached Santiago de Cuba.
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, 'The Revolution Begins Now', speech at Cespedes Park, Santiago de Cuba, 3 January 1959 (Marxists Internet Archive translation)
sources: Marxists Internet Archive, Castro archive, 3 January 1959
suggested_refs: The balcony of the Ayuntamiento over Parque Cespedes, Santiago de Cuba

stops.name: La Cabana, Havana: the tribunals
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the corpus interlock
stops.campa: Guevara takes the eighteenth-century fortress across the harbor from Havana, and with it the machinery of the old regime's punishment. Acting for a government Castro has not yet formally joined, he presides over the revolutionary tribunals that try Batista's police, torturers and informers, and several hundred are shot at the moat wall in the first months. The counts are disputed from every direction. Castro answers the foreign press by holding one trial in a sports stadium before seventeen thousand people.
suggested_refs: The moat wall of the Fortaleza de San Carlos de la Cabana

stops.name: Havana: Camp Columbia and the doves
stops.date_confidence: corrected: the pool's chronology lens said 9 January and contradicted its own geography lens; Wikipedia's Habana Libre article and the universal dating of the Camp Columbia address both give the night of 8 January 1959
stops.campa: The caravan from Santiago takes eight days to cross the island, stopping in every town it passes, and reaches the capital on the eighth of January. Castro speaks that night from the military headquarters of the regime he has destroyed, in fatigues, for hours, and white doves are released over the platform; one settles on his shoulder and stays. Santeros in the crowd read it as the sign of Obatala. He turns to Camilo Cienfuegos and asks whether he is doing all right, and the answer goes out over the island: you are doing fine, Fidel.
suggested_refs: Camp Columbia, Havana, converted after 1959 into the Ciudad Libertad school city

stops.name: Habana Libre, Vedado: room 2324
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the first press conference in the ballroom; the pool's coordinate was 400 m north of the building and has been corrected
stops.campa: Rather than the presidential palace he takes the Continental Suite, room 2324, on the twenty-third floor of what was the Havana Hilton until the revolution took it, and runs the country from a hotel for three months. He holds his first press conference in the ballroom on the nineteenth of January. The lobby fills with petitioners, reporters and armed men. Later he keeps the Castellana Suite, room 2224, which is preserved as a museum. A government out of the Sierra installs itself in the newest building in Havana and does not unpack.
suggested_refs: The Castellana Suite, room 2224, Hotel Habana Libre, preserved as a museum

stops.name: Havana: sworn in as prime minister
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Jose Miro Cardona resigns and Castro is sworn in as prime minister, six weeks after entering Havana, under the provisional president Manuel Urrutia. Until now he has held no office but commander of the rebel armed forces, which is the only office that counts. In April he answers the question of when the promised elections will come: revolution first, elections later. Cuba will not hold a competitive national vote again in his lifetime. He is thirty-two years old, and he will govern for forty-nine years.
suggested_refs: The oath of office of 16 February 1959, Havana

stops.name: United States Capitol, Washington: Nixon takes his measure
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day not given in the pool; the Princeton talk of 20 April 1959 and the zoo visit fall inside the same trip
stops.campa: Invited by American newspaper editors rather than by the government, he arrives in fatigues on what his people call Operation Truth. Eisenhower goes golfing. Nixon receives him for two and a half hours and writes afterward that the man is either extraordinarily naive about communism or under its discipline. Castro tells everyone who asks that he has not come for money. He lays a wreath at the Lincoln Memorial, speaks to students at Princeton, and is photographed feeding an elephant at the Central Park zoo, a scene the press cameras keep and no record confirms.
sources: Princeton University archival accounts (cited, not fetched)
suggested_refs: The April 1959 Operation Truth tour of the United States

stops.name: Havana: the First Agrarian Reform Law
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day not given in the pool and defaulted to the first
stops.campa: The First Agrarian Reform Law caps landholdings at nine hundred and ninety-three acres, forbids foreign ownership of farmland, and sets up the National Institute of Agrarian Reform to move the rest. Something near fifteen percent of the national wealth changes hands inside the year. The law strikes the American sugar companies and the Cuban landowning class in the same clause, and among the estates taken is the Castro family finca at Biran. His mother is said to have asked him what he thought he was doing. Washington answers with sugar quotas.
suggested_refs: The Instituto Nacional de Reforma Agraria and the law of May 1959

stops.name: Buenos Aires: thirty billion dollars, refused
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day not given in the pool; the canonical corpus coordinate for Buenos Aires is inherited unchanged
stops.campa: He flies to the inter-American economic conference and asks the hemisphere for thirty billion dollars of United States development aid over ten years, a Marshall Plan for Latin America, and is refused. The delegates hear a man in uniform propose the alternative to the course he is about to take. This is the city where Ernesto Guevara was born and took his medical degree before the road that led to Mexico. Castro leaves with nothing and goes home to nationalize.
suggested_refs: The 1959 inter-American economic conference, Buenos Aires

stops.name: Camaguey: the arrest of Huber Matos
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: The military commander of Camaguey, a rice farmer who fought in the Sierra, resigns in a letter protesting the growing communist presence in the army. Castro sends Camilo Cienfuegos to arrest him unarmed in front of his own men, then calls a rally in Havana demanding revolutionary tribunals for treason. Matos is given twenty years and serves every one of them. Three months earlier Castro had resigned the premiership over Urrutia's anti-communism and taken it back within days. Nine days after Camaguey, Cienfuegos's aircraft vanishes over the sea.
suggested_refs: Huber Matos's resignation letter of 19 October 1959

stops.name: Havana: a good economist
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the corpus interlock
stops.campa: Castro asks a room of comandantes whether there is a good economist among them and Guevara raises his hand; by his own later account he had heard a good communist. Guevara has no training in economics. He is made president of the National Bank of Cuba and signs the new banknotes simply Che, which Havana reads as contempt for money and New York reads as a statement of intent. Within a year the banks, the refineries, the sugar mills and the telephone company are property of the Cuban state.
suggested_refs: Cuban banknotes of 1960 signed Che

stops.name: Havana harbor: La Coubre, patria o muerte
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the corpus interlock
stops.campa: A French freighter carrying Belgian munitions explodes at the Havana docks and explodes a second time as the rescuers reach it; about a hundred are killed. Castro accuses the United States without evidence and buries the dead the next day in a procession along the Malecon. Over the coffins he first uses the words that become the motto of the state: patria o muerte, homeland or death. On the platform Alberto Korda takes one frame of Guevara looking past the camera, prints it, and files it away for seven years.
suggested_refs: Korda's Guerrillero Heroico, exposed at the La Coubre funeral, 5 March 1960

stops.name: United Nations, New York: four hours and twenty-nine minutes
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Refused by a midtown hotel over a cash deposit, the Cuban delegation moves to the Hotel Theresa in Harlem, where Khrushchev comes uptown to embrace him in the lobby and Nasser, Nehru and Malcolm X come to call. At the General Assembly he speaks for four hours and twenty-nine minutes, the longest address the body has ever heard, and opens by promising to be brief. The story that the delegation plucked chickens in the rooms is tabloid and has never been sourced. Within four months Washington breaks off relations.
stops.quote: Although it has been said of us that we speak at great length, you may rest assured that we shall endeavor to be brief.
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, address to the United Nations General Assembly, New York, 26 September 1960 (Marxists Internet Archive translation)
sources: Marxists Internet Archive, Castro archive, 26 September 1960
suggested_refs: The Hotel Theresa, 125th Street and Seventh Avenue, Harlem

stops.name: Playa Giron: seventy-two hours
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the pool's coordinate fell 10 km out in open water and has been corrected to the village on the eastern bank
stops.campa: Fourteen hundred exiles of Brigade 2506 land in the swamp on the eastern shore of the Bay of Pigs and find the militia awake and the promised air cover cancelled. Castro directs the fight from a sugar mill at Central Australia and drives down to the beach himself, riding on a tank. It is finished in three days; twelve hundred prisoners are taken and later ransomed for baby food and medicine. At a funeral the day before the landings, standing in front of anti-aircraft guns, he had already declared the revolution socialist.
stops.quote: in less than 72 hours we have destroyed the invasion which was prepared by the brains of the Pentagon with all the tactics and preparations of a war.
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, 'Denouncing U.S. Bay of Pigs Invasion', Havana, 23 April 1961 (Marxists Internet Archive translation)
sources: Marxists Internet Archive, Castro archive, 23 April 1961
suggested_refs: The Museo Giron at Playa Giron, Matanzas

stops.name: Cuba: the missiles
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day not given in the pool and defaulted to the first
stops.campa: Soviet medium-range missiles are photographed on the island and for thirteen days the world holds still. Castro is not meaningfully consulted about their installation and is not consulted at all about their removal; he learns of Khrushchev's agreement with Kennedy from the radio. In the worst hour he writes to Moscow urging a first strike if the Americans invade, a letter he will spend decades explaining. He is left holding a guarantee against invasion that he did not negotiate and a patron he can no longer entirely trust.
suggested_refs: The U-2 photographs of the San Cristobal missile sites, October 1962

stops.name: The Kremlin, Moscow: thirty-eight days
stops.date_confidence: attested; the pool's range ended in May and has been corrected, the visit running 27 April to 3 June 1963
stops.campa: He goes to the Soviet Union for the first time and stays thirty-eight days, through factories and collective farms and Siberia, standing on the Lenin mausoleum for May Day and made a Hero of the Soviet Union. Khrushchev flatters him for weeks and the missiles are not discussed in public. Six years earlier in this city Mao Zedong told the assembled parties that the east wind prevails over the west wind, and the quarrel that opened there now runs through Havana as well. Castro will not settle between Moscow and Peking until the decade is nearly out.
suggested_refs: The 1963 May Day parade on Red Square, Castro on the mausoleum

segments.name: The Long Reign and the Ashes

stops.name: Jose Marti airport, Havana: forty hours
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by the corpus interlock
stops.campa: Guevara comes back from Algiers, where he attacked the Soviet bloc for buying from the poor world at market prices, and Castro meets him at the airport with Raul and Dorticos. The two men go into a room and talk for forty hours. Guevara is never seen in public in Cuba again. On the third of October Castro reads aloud to the new Central Committee the letter in which Guevara gives up his rank, his ministries and his Cuban citizenship, and says that other lands are calling for his modest efforts.
suggested_refs: Guevara's farewell letter of 1 April 1965, read aloud in Havana on 3 October

stops.name: La Moneda, Santiago de Chile: twenty-four days
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day of arrival; the pool's twenty-three days has been corrected to the 10 November to 4 December span, which some accounts give as twenty-five
stops.campa: Salvador Allende receives him at the palace and Castro stays twenty-four days, from the copper pit at Chuquicamata to Tierra del Fuego, longer than any foreign head of government has stayed anywhere. He warns Chilean audiences that a revolution made at the ballot box has no army of its own. Two years later the palace is bombed and Allende dies inside it, and Augusto Pinochet, who was posted at Antofagasta on desert this tour crossed, takes the country. Havana opens its doors to those who get out.
sources: Wikipedia (es), 'Visita de Fidel Castro a Chile'

stops.name: Luanda: Operation Carlota
stops.date_confidence: year attested; the pool gives no month, defaulted to January, though the airlift belongs to the last months of 1975
stops.campa: Cuban troops fly to Angola to hold Luanda for the MPLA against South African columns coming up from the south. Castro plans it in Havana and names it Operation Carlota, after a slave who led a rising in Matanzas. Moscow does not ask for it and is told late. Cuban units will go on to fight in the Ogaden for Ethiopia and to hold Cuito Cuanavale in 1988, and at the peak as many as fifty thousand Cubans are in Africa at once, sent from an island of six million people.

stops.name: Palacio de las Convenciones, Havana: the Non-Aligned
stops.date_confidence: month attested, day not given in the pool and defaulted to the first; the venue is tagged as reconstruction in the pool
stops.campa: He hosts the sixth summit of the Non-Aligned Movement and takes its chair for three years, arguing to the assembled poor world that the socialist bloc is its natural ally rather than a second imperialism. Tito and others refuse the formula. In October he addresses the United Nations General Assembly as chairman, on debt and hunger, and is applauded by a hall that will not follow him. Two months after that the Soviet army goes into Afghanistan and leaves him defending it before the same movement.

stops.name: CIMEQ, Siboney: the surgery
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the hospital was never officially named and the coordinate is a placeholder for the Siboney district
stops.campa: Intestinal surgery for a bleeding he has hidden for months forces him to sign a provisional transfer of the presidency to his brother, the first interruption of his rule in forty-seven years. He does not appear in public for months, and is photographed in a tracksuit holding a newspaper to prove the date. The Soviet Union went in 1991 and took eighty percent of Cuban trade with it, and the island has already chewed through the years it calls the Special Period. He resigns the presidency in 2008 and the party in 2011.
suggested_refs: The photographs of Castro with a dated newspaper, autumn 2006

stops.name: Palacio de las Convenciones, Havana: the seventh congress
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Frail, in a blue tracksuit, he addresses the closing session of the party congress from a chair, and the delegates stand. He tells them this may be the last time he speaks in this hall and that the ideas of Cuban communists will remain. Barack Obama had walked through Old Havana a month before, and Castro had answered him in the newspaper by saying that Cuba needs no gifts from the empire. He is eighty-nine years old. Most of the men in the room with him are in their eighties too.
stops.quote: I'll soon be 90 years old... Soon I'll be like all the others; to all of us our turn must come.
stops.quote_source: Fidel Castro, closing address to the Seventh Congress of the Communist Party of Cuba, Havana, 19 April 2016
sources: Contemporary press coverage of the 19 April 2016 speech

stops.name: Havana: the death and the ashes
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and the hour, 22:29
stops.campa: He dies at half past ten at night at the age of ninety, and Raul reads a short statement on television. The body is cremated the next morning in a private ceremony, so that there is no corpse to embalm and set out; the man who filled the Plaza de la Revolucion for fifty years leaves it nothing to look at. The urn lies in state at the Jose Marti memorial and the crowds file past for two days. Raul announces that there will be no statues of his brother, no busts, and no street bearing his name.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Fidel Castro'

stops.name: Santa Ifigenia Cemetery, Santiago de Cuba: one word
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and to seven in the morning
stops.campa: The ashes travel nine hundred kilometers from Havana to Santiago over four days, retracing the caravan of January 1959 in reverse, through the towns that lined the road the first time. On the way the vehicle carrying them breaks down and soldiers push it. At seven in the morning, with the press shut out, the urn is set into a granite boulder in the cemetery where Jose Marti lies, under one word: FIDEL. No dates, no surname, no rank. The state that forbids his statues has given him a stone with a name on it.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Death and state funeral of Fidel Castro'
